biological.citation: Ey/Schmeisser et al. 2012 - Autistic-like behaviours and hyperactivity in mice lacking ProSAP1/Shank2 (PMID: 22699619)
biological.summary: Shank2 knockout mice show early, brain-region-specific upregulation of synaptic ionotropic glutamate receptors and increased Shank3. They also have fewer dendritic spines, reduced basal synaptic transmission, lower mEPSC frequency and enhanced NMDAR currents. Behaviorally they are hyperactive with repetitive grooming and abnormal vocal and social behavior.

biological.citation: Early Correction of NMDA Receptor Function Improves Autistic-like Social Behaviors in Adult Shank2-/- Mice (PMID: 30466882)
biological.summary: Shank2-/- (exon 6-7 deletion) mice show NMDAR hyperfunction at ~P14 that shifts to NMDAR hypofunction after weaning. Chronic memantine given at P7-P21 prevents the later NMDAR hypofunction and autistic-like social deficits.

biological.citation: Enhancing inhibitory synaptic function reverses spatial memory deficits in Shank2 mutant mice (PMID: 27544825)
biological.summary: Gabra2 expression and GABA receptor-mediated inhibitory transmission are reduced in Shank2 e6-7 KO mice but not in e7 KO mice. An allosteric GABAA receptor modulator reverses the spatial memory deficits in e6-7 KO mice.

biological.citation: Shank2 mutant mice display a hypersecretory response to cholera toxin (PMID: 24445315)
biological.summary: A long Shank2 isoform (Shank2E) is predominantly expressed in pancreatic, renal and intestinal epithelia. Shank2 forms a CFTR-Shank2-PDE4D complex, and its deletion raised CFTR-dependent short-circuit currents by 84% in colon and 101% in rectum. Cholera toxin-induced fluid accumulation rose by ~90% in the intestine.

biological.citation: SHANK2 establishes auditory hair bundle architecture essential for mammalian hearing (PMID: 40627398)
biological.summary: SHANK2 localizes to the medial apical surface of developing cochlear hair cells, and this localization depends on the small GTPase RAP1. It acts independently of the Gαi/GPSM2 and aPKCζ/PARD6B polarity proteins. Hair cell-specific Shank2 or Rap1 ablation disrupts bundle architecture, causing loss of OHC V-shape, impaired high-frequency amplification, and progressive degeneration and hearing loss.

biological.citation: Somatic structural variation targets neurodevelopmental genes and identifies SHANK2 as a tumor suppressor in neuroblastoma (PMID: 32796005)
biological.summary: SHANK2 was disrupted by somatic SVs in 14% of MYCN-nonamplified high-risk tumors by WGS and in 10% in the SNP array cohort. Its expression is low in neuroblastoma cell lines and high-risk tumors. Forced SHANK2 expression inhibited neuroblastoma cell growth and accelerated retinoic acid-induced neuronal differentiation.
biological.significance: growth inhibition P=2.6e-2 to 3.4e-5; differentiation P=3.1e-13 to 2.4e-30

biological.citation: Genetic and functional analyses of SHANK2 mutations suggest a multiple hit model of autism spectrum disorders (PMID: 22346768)
biological.summary: A novel 421 kb de novo SHANK2 deletion was found in an ASD patient. Variants affecting conserved amino acids were enriched in patients (3.4%) versus controls (1.5%). In neuronal cultures, patient variants reduced synaptic density at dendrites compared with control-only variants. De novo deletion carriers also had inherited 15q11-q13 CNVs involving CHRNA7 or CYFIP1.
biological.sample_size: 455 patients and 431 controls (851 patients and 1,090 controls combined)

biological.citation: Behavioral and Sensory Deficits Associated with Dysfunction of GABAergic System in a Novel shank2-Deficient Zebrafish Model (PMID: 36768529)
biological.summary: shank2b-/- zebrafish show reduced social and kin preference, stereotypy, auditory hypersensitivity and hyperactivity. They also have reduced GABA receptor subunit mRNA and protein and greater sensitivity to drug-induced seizures, implicating GABAergic dysfunction in sensory hyper-reactivity.

biological.citation: Identification of a novel Shank2 transcriptional variant in Shank2 knockout mouse model of autism spectrum disorder (PMID: 32252796)
biological.summary: RNA-seq of Shank2 e6-7 KO mice revealed prominent expression of a novel exon 4' between exons 4 and 5. The variant was confirmed by RT-PCR and western blot and may act as a modifier explaining phenotypic differences between the e6-7 and e7 KO lines (genetic compensation).

biological.citation: ASHG 2022 - Extensive Transcriptional Complexity of Autism Associated SHANK Family Genes by Capture Based and Long Read sequencing Method
biological.summary: Long-read Iso-Seq found ~350 Shank1/Shank2 isoforms in mouse cortex and ~200 in striatum, and ~500 SHANK1-3 isoforms in human. The domain combination of SAM, SH3 and ANK was seen only for SHANK1, not SHANK2 or SHANK3. Novel exons, fusion transcripts, alternative promoters and cell-type-specific isoform usage were also reported.
